title: DVR Labs Polaroid Stack - Fling-to-Shuffle Photo Pile

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A pile of instant photos lying at their own casual angles on a desk; you fling the top one aside and it lands underneath the pile.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: A gallery where the top photo can be flung: it slides off with the throw's velocity, tucks in behind the stack, and the next photo becomes active - browsing by reshuffling the pile instead of paging through a carousel.

design_tokens.borders: White instant-photo frames with slight per-item rotation
design_tokens.elevation: Stacked depth via rotation offsets and small shadow separation between layers
design_tokens.typography: Handwritten captions under photos; minimal supporting UI type

interactive_mechanics: Fling the top photo - velocity carries it off and it tucks behind the stack
Per-photo resting rotation for a naturally untidy pile
usability_notes: Fling-to-cycle replaces prev/next buttons with one gesture that reads as reshuffling rather than navigation - good for small personal galleries where serendipity beats completeness. Keep piles short (the stack hides content depth; a counter or thumbnails preserve orientation), mirror the fling for RTL locales, and give keyboard/AT users a plain list alternative. Same-author sibling to ref-005/ref-007 (DVR Labs); source: component page description.
